summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA (published 2026-09-20) covers Lucid's partnership with European ride-hailing platform Bolt to deploy at least 25,000 autonomous vehicles across major European cities — news that sent LCID up over 9% that day. He frames this as Lucid's second major AV-fleet deal after a similar Uber agreement, and argues Lucid is well positioned: its technology is best-in-class on efficiency (miles per kWh), with the Gravity SUV beating rivals like Cadillac's Escalade IQ on range despite a smaller battery — a critical cost advantage for fleet operators. Lucid has also licensed its tech to Aston Martin. The counterweight is severe financial distress: the business was built for ~100,000 units/year but sells under 20,000 EVs annually, and he estimates free cash flow of negative $4 billion in 2026, -$2.7B in 2027, -$1.5B in 2028, -$460M in 2029, reaching breakeven only in 2030. He values the business at about $0.70/share versus a $4.28 market price and warns of Fisker-style bankruptcy risk deterring buyers. Conclusion: not a buying opportunity yet despite the good news. Call: LCID AVOID @ $4.28.
